name: Jordan Lin
headline: Security Analyst | Applied ML for Threat Detection
summary: Security analyst with hands-on SOC experience and graduate research in machine learning for intrusion detection.

bullets.text: Triaged 40+ Splunk alerts per shift and escalated confirmed incidents following the IR playbook.
Wrote 12 Sigma detection rules for credential-stuffing and impossible-travel patterns, cutting false positives by 38%.
Automated phishing-report enrichment with Python and the VirusTotal API, reducing analyst handling time from 15 to 4 minutes per report.
bullets.context: The script pulled URL and attachment verdicts and posted a summary to the ServiceNow ticket; the Tier 1 team used it for every reported phish.

bullets.text: Documented 5 runbooks for the Tier 1 team.
Trained gradient-boosted and LSTM models on CIC-IDS2017 network flows, reaching 0.97 F1 on held-out traffic.
Evaluated adversarial evasion attacks against the intrusion-detection models using the Adversarial Robustness Toolbox.
Co-authored a workshop paper on robustness of ML-based intrusion detection.
Resolved 300+ help-desk tickets covering account lockouts, MFA enrollment and printer issues.
Imaged and patched 60 lab workstations each semester using Microsoft Intune.
Built a harness that replays 250 prompt-injection payloads against LLM apps and scores responses for policy violations.
Mapped findings to the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications.
Deployed Wazuh and Suricata on a Proxmox cluster to practice detection engineering against simulated attacks from Atomic Red Team.
Fine-tuned a DistilBERT classifier on 20,000 labeled emails, achieving 94% accuracy.

details: Coursework: Network Security, Machine Learning, Digital Forensics

extra.text: Taught weekly cyber-hygiene workshops for seniors at the Austin Public Library in 2023.
